sam.belief: He saw a tall shape beside Reservoir Road after his bus route, in poor visibility; he remains the only person reporting a sighting.
sam.stance: Keeps Longshape as a cautious description and wants his report left on record. He knows Harold and Ellen have not seen what he reported.

harold.belief: He has never seen anything and doubts Sam identified anything at all.
harold.stance: Still favors Roadside Case as a practical label for the report. He does not claim that his proposed name identifies an animal.

ellen.belief: She has never seen anything and wants evidence before accepting a more specific term.
ellen.stance: Still favors Unverified Form because it marks uncertainty and does not turn a description into an established proper name.

public_record.headline: Sam Evers proposes "Longshape" as name for reservoir animal
Harold Vale and Ellen Price dispute Sam Evers' proposed name
Reservoir animal naming debate draws community comment

turns.text: Sam, why “Longshape”?
It says what I saw without claiming what it was.
It says very little. A useful label ought to help someone sort one thing from another.
That assumes there is a thing to sort. Sam reported a shape.
I reported what I could see in poor visibility.
And I am not saying you saw nothing. I am saying the label should wait.
I agree about waiting. I do not agree that “Longshape” is a proper name.
You both want a better name, but neither of you has seen it.
Correct. That is why I’m asking for a practical standard first.
And I am asking that we distinguish a description from a name.
For now, I’d rather use a modest word than pretend I know more.
The station will keep the proposal on record, without upgrading it to an identification.
Harold, what does Roadside Case help you do?
Put the report somewhere findable. A label should work on a folder.
A folder can hold a report without deciding there is a case.
That is why I said case, not creature.
Longshape still describes what I could make out. I am not claiming more than that.
Unverified Form keeps the uncertainty attached to the words.
It sounds like a box on a form that has not been filled in.
That would be an accurate use of the phrase.
So far, the names are competing; the evidence is not.
I can live with that, provided my report stays on record.
Keep the report. I still want a label that sorts properly.
And I want the label to say what we actually know.
We have three proposed labels and no agreement. Sam, are you still using yours?
Yes. Longshape stays close to what I could make out.
For filing, I still think Roadside Case is clearer. It tells you where the report belongs.
It tells you there is a case. Unverified Form keeps the uncertainty in plain view.
A form can be unverified without becoming the title of the folder.
And a folder title can sound more conclusive than its contents.
I’m not asking either of you to endorse what I saw. I’m asking that the description remain mine.
Would you accept the three names listed side by side?
Side by side is workable, provided nobody files them as three separate reports.
That is a sensible distinction. Names are not evidence.
Then Longshape can stay as my description, not a finding.
The station will keep the disagreement as a disagreement.
